_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Cyprus covering Bronze Age Alashiya (copper trade), Mycenaean-Achaean colonisation, Phoenician Kition, Assyrian/Egyptian/Persian rule, Hellenistic Ptolemaic period, Roman province (Paphos), Byzantine era, Richard the Lionheart/Lusignan Crusader kingdom, Venetian rule, Ottoman conquest 1571, British colony 1878, EOKA/Enosis, independence 1960, intercommunal violence, Turkish invasion 1974, division (Green Line), EU accession 2004 (acquis suspended for north), and reunification talks.

country_profile.capital: Nicosia (Lefkosia/Lefkoşa) — last divided capital in Europe
country_profile.government_type: Unitary presidential constitutional republic (de facto divided: Republic of Cyprus controls south; Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in north, recognised only by Türkiye)
country_profile.currency: Euro (EUR, south since 2008) / Turkish lira (TRY, north)

religion.note: Greek Orthodox (south) and Sunni Muslim (north) broadly correlate with Greek/Turkish communities

ethnic_groups.name: Greek Cypriot
ethnic_groups.notes: Greek-speaking; Orthodox Christian; southern Cyprus; claim descent from Mycenaean/Achaean settlers; enosis (union with Greece) was historic aspiration

ethnic_groups.name: Turkish Cypriot
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkish-speaking; Sunni Muslim; northern Cyprus; arrived during Ottoman period (1571+); TRNC since 1983; augmented by mainland Turkish settlers post-1974

ethnic_groups.name: Maronite
ethnic_groups.notes: Recognized minority; Kormakitis/Korucam; Aramaic (Cypriot Maronite Arabic); Catholic; villages in north

ethnic_groups.name: Armenian
ethnic_groups.notes: Refugee descendants from 1915 Genocide; Nicosia; Armenian Apostolic

ethnic_groups.name: Latin (Levantine)
ethnic_groups.notes: Catholic; remnant of Lusignan/Venetian period; Limassol/Larnaca

ethnic_groups.name: Other (British, Russian, Filipino, Sri Lankan, South Asian)
ethnic_groups.notes: British residents (2 Sovereign Base Areas: Akrotiri and Dhekelia); Russian/Eastern European community in Limassol; expat workers

country_profile.notes_unique: Only divided EU member state; Varosha (Fenced city since 1974); Aphrodite's legendary birthplace (Petra tou Romiou); oldest named wine (Commandaria); 2 UK Sovereign Base Areas

current_leader.name: Nikos Christodoulides
current_leader.title: President (Republic of Cyprus)
current_leader.notes: Independent; former foreign minister; supports federal solution for reunification

trnc_leader.name: Ersin Tatar
trnc_leader.title: President (TRNC, internationally unrecognised)
trnc_leader.notes: Favours two-state solution; backed by Türkiye

former_leaders.name: Archbishop Makarios III
former_leaders.notes: First president; ethnarch; Greek Orthodox Archbishop; survived EOKA-B/Greek junta coup July 1974 (trigger for Turkish invasion); died August 1977

former_leaders.name: Glafcos Clerides
former_leaders.notes: DISY; EOKA veteran; negotiated with Turkish side; EU accession process

former_leaders.name: Tassos Papadopoulos
former_leaders.notes: DIKO; led campaign against Annan Plan (2004 referendum: Greek side rejected 75.8% no)

910.name: Bronze Age Cyprus and Alashiya
910.description: Cyprus as one of the earliest centers of copper metallurgy, known as Alashiya in Near Eastern texts, its role in the Late Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean trade network, and the Bronze Age collapse.

sub_clusters.name: Copper Metallurgy and Early Settlements
sub_clusters.description: The Chalcolithic and Early Bronze Age societies of Cyprus, the exploitation of copper deposits that gave the island its name, and the development of distinctive Cypriot pottery traditions.
key_events: Cyprus becomes a major copper producer, its name possibly the root of the Latin 'cuprum' (copper)

sub_clusters.name: Late Bronze Age Alashiya
sub_clusters.description: Cyprus as Alashiya, a kingdom in diplomatic correspondence with Egypt and the Hittites, the wealthy trading city of Enkomi, Mycenaean Greek settlement, and the devastation of the Bronze Age collapse.

910.name: Iron Age City-Kingdoms
910.description: The Cypriot city-kingdoms of the Iron Age — Salamis, Kition, Paphos, Amathus — under Assyrian, Egyptian, Persian, and Ptolemaic rule, and the island's cultural synthesis of Greek and Near Eastern traditions.

sub_clusters.name: Cypriot City-Kingdoms and Assyrian-Persian Rule
sub_clusters.description: The ten independent Cypriot kingdoms, their tribute to Assyria, the Ionian Revolt participation, and the island's strategic importance to successive Near Eastern empires.
key_events: Cypriot kingdoms submit to Assyria under Sargon II (c. 709 BC)
Cypriot cities join the Ionian Revolt against Persia (499 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Hellenistic and Ptolemaic Cyprus
sub_clusters.description: Alexander's conquest, the abolition of city-kingdoms by Ptolemy I, three centuries of Ptolemaic Egyptian rule, the cult of Aphrodite at Paphos, and the island's annexation by Rome.

910.name: Roman Cyprus
910.description: Cyprus as a Roman senatorial province, the apostolic missions of Paul and Barnabas, the devastating Kitos War Jewish revolt, and the major earthquakes reshaping the island's cities.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Administration and Christianity
sub_clusters.description: Roman provincial governance, the mission of St. Paul and St. Barnabas making Cyprus one of the first regions to adopt Christianity, the Kitos War destruction, and the earthquakes that destroyed Salamis and Paphos.
key_events: Apostles Paul and Barnabas convert the Roman governor Sergius Paulus (c. 45 AD)
Kitos War — massive Jewish revolt devastates Salamis (115–117 AD)

920.name: Byzantine Cyprus
920.description: Cyprus under Byzantine rule, the unique Arab-Byzantine condominium, the autocephaly of the Church of Cyprus, and the island's role between the Christian and Muslim worlds.

sub_clusters.name: Early Byzantine and Arab Raids
sub_clusters.description: Byzantine administration, the granting of autocephaly to the Church of Cyprus at the Council of Ephesus, and the devastating Arab raids that began under Muawiya.

sub_clusters.name: Arab-Byzantine Condominium
sub_clusters.description: The unique arrangement under which Cyprus was jointly governed by the Byzantine and Umayyad/Abbasid empires, sharing tax revenues — a rare example of medieval peaceful coexistence.

sub_clusters.name: Return to Full Byzantine Control
sub_clusters.description: Nikephoros Phokas' reconquest ending the condominium, the island's reintegration into the Byzantine theme system, and the period leading to the Third Crusade.

920.name: Lusignan Crusader Kingdom of Cyprus
920.description: Richard the Lionheart's conquest, the Lusignan dynasty's feudal Latin kingdom, Famagusta's rise as the wealthiest city in the eastern Mediterranean, and the Venetian takeover.

sub_clusters.name: Richard the Lionheart and Lusignan Establishment
sub_clusters.description: Richard I's seizure of Cyprus during the Third Crusade, its sale to the Knights Templar and then Guy de Lusignan, and the establishment of a feudal Latin kingdom with French-speaking aristocracy.
key_events: Richard the Lionheart conquers Cyprus en route to the Third Crusade (1191)
Guy de Lusignan establishes the Lusignan dynasty on Cyprus (1192)

sub_clusters.name: Famagusta's Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The fall of Acre drives Christian merchants to Famagusta, making it the wealthiest city in the eastern Mediterranean, its 365 churches, and the disastrous Genoese invasion.

sub_clusters.name: Venetian Takeover
sub_clusters.description: Queen Caterina Cornaro's abdication under Venetian pressure, the annexation of Cyprus by the Republic of Venice, and the fortification of Nicosia and Famagusta.

930.name: Venetian and Ottoman Cyprus
930.description: Venetian colonial rule, the Ottoman conquest of 1570–1571, the siege of Famagusta, and three centuries of Ottoman administration transforming the island's demographics and culture.

sub_clusters.name: Venetian Rule and Ottoman Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Venetian fortification of the island, the Ottoman invasion ordered by Selim II, the heroic but doomed defense of Famagusta by Marcantonio Bragadin, and the Ottoman victory.
key_events: Ottoman forces besiege and capture Nicosia in a single assault (1570)
Fall of Famagusta after 11-month siege; Bragadin flayed alive (1571)

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Administration
sub_clusters.description: The Ottoman millet system restoring the Orthodox Church's authority, Muslim settlement, the development of a Turkish Cypriot community, and the Archbishop's role as ethnarch of Greek Cypriots.

940.name: Late Ottoman and British Acquisition
940.description: The 1821 Greek uprising's impact on Cyprus, the British lease of Cyprus from the Ottomans in 1878, and the beginnings of the enosis (union with Greece) movement.

sub_clusters.name: Greek Revolution Impact and Late Ottoman Era
sub_clusters.description: The Ottoman execution of Archbishop Kyprianos and Greek Cypriot notables during the 1821 Greek War of Independence, and growing communal tensions.
key_events: Archbishop Kyprianos and Greek Cypriot leaders executed by Ottomans (1821)

sub_clusters.name: British Administration Begins
sub_clusters.description: The Cyprus Convention giving Britain administrative control in exchange for Ottoman defense guarantees, British colonial governance, and the rise of Greek Cypriot enosis aspirations.

940.name: British Crown Colony
940.description: Cyprus as a British Crown Colony, the 1931 uprising, EOKA's guerrilla campaign for enosis, the Turkish Cypriot counter-movement for taksim (partition), and the road to independence.

sub_clusters.name: Crown Colony and 1931 Revolt
sub_clusters.description: British annexation during WWI, the 1931 Greek Cypriot uprising against colonial rule, the burning of Government House, and repressive British measures.

sub_clusters.name: EOKA Campaign and Independence
sub_clusters.description: EOKA's armed guerrilla struggle for enosis led by Grivas, the TMT Turkish Cypriot counter-movement, Archbishop Makarios' exile, and the Zurich-London Agreements creating the Republic of Cyprus.
key_events: EOKA begins armed campaign for union with Greece (April 1, 1955)
Republic of Cyprus declared independent under the Zurich-London agreements (1960)

950.name: Republic of Cyprus and Intercommunal Conflict
950.description: The fragile Republic of Cyprus under President Makarios, the constitutional crisis, intercommunal violence, the Greek junta-backed coup, and the Turkish invasion and partition.

sub_clusters.name: Constitutional Crisis and Intercommunal Violence
sub_clusters.description: The Makarios-proposed constitutional amendments, the 1963 'Bloody Christmas' intercommunal fighting, the withdrawal of Turkish Cypriots into enclaves, and UN peacekeeping deployment.

sub_clusters.name: 1974 Coup and Turkish Invasion
sub_clusters.description: The Greek junta-backed EOKA-B coup against Makarios, Turkey's military intervention citing its guarantor powers, the de facto partition of the island, and the displacement of 200,000 Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
key_events: Greek junta-backed coup d'état deposes President Makarios (July 15, 1974)
Turkey launches military intervention; island is divided along the Green Line (July 20, 1974)

960.name: Divided Cyprus and EU Accession
960.description: The divided island — the Republic of Cyprus in the south and the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus — the failed Annan Plan, EU membership, and ongoing reunification efforts.

sub_clusters.name: TRNC Declaration and International Isolation
sub_clusters.description: The unilateral declaration of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus recognized only by Turkey, the economic embargo, and decades of frozen diplomatic impasse.

sub_clusters.name: Annan Plan and EU Accession
sub_clusters.description: The UN Annan Plan referenda — accepted by Turkish Cypriots but rejected by Greek Cypriots — and the Republic of Cyprus joining the EU as a divided island.
key_events: Annan Plan referendum: Turkish Cypriots vote yes, Greek Cypriots vote no (April 2004)
Republic of Cyprus joins the European Union (May 1, 2004)

sub_clusters.name: Post-EU Accession and Reunification Talks
sub_clusters.description: The collapse of the Crans-Montana talks in 2017, the discovery of Eastern Mediterranean gas deposits complicating geopolitics, and the ongoing impasse over reunification.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
